_meta.purpose: STOF CSRF Vulnerability Knowledge Base -- real-world attack patterns for stof/modules/csrf_tests.py.
sources: PortSwigger Web Security Academy -- CSRF where token is not tied to user session, Bypassing CSRF token validation
HackerOne #182487 (GitLab) -- account-deletion CSRF token bypassed by substituting a token minted for a different account
HackTricks CSRF guide -- method override / content-type downgrade bypasses
_meta.key_finding: csrf_tests.py covers five CSRF gaps: no token field at all (TC-130.1), token presence not actually validated (TC-130.2), Origin/Referer not validated (TC-130.3), token not bound to the presenting session (TC-130.4), and SameSite-attribute CSRF relevance (TC-130.5, framed distinctly from session_weakness_tests.py's TC-129.5 session-hijacking angle on the same cookie attribute -- FAILs only on an unconditional SameSite=None gap or a Lax/absent SameSite compounding with this module's OWN already-confirmed TC-130.1+TC-130.3 gaps on the same endpoint). A sixth technique, content-type-switch bypass (TC-130.6), was re-verified this session against api_sniffer.py's actual JSON-body-detection logic: it is buildable and implemented, but SKIPs cleanly on any target with no discovered JSON-body-shaped API endpoint -- a classic form-POST target like demo.testfire.net is expected to always take this SKIP path, which is not a bug.

patterns.generalized_transformation: Authenticate as a low-privilege attacker-controlled account (role A), GET the target state-changing form to harvest its own, syntactically valid, freshly-issued anti-CSRF token. Submit the SAME state-changing POST -- using a DIFFERENT session's (role B's) cookies -- with role A's harvested token value in the token field, instead of a token that actually belongs to role B's session.
patterns.abstracted_endpoint_pattern: Any state-changing POST form endpoint whose anti-CSRF token is validated for well-formedness/existence in some server-side store, but not cross-checked against the specific session presenting it.
patterns.real_example: PortSwigger's 'CSRF where token is not tied to user session' lab; HackerOne #182487 (GitLab) where an account-deletion request's CSRF token, harvested from one account, was accepted when replayed against a different account's session.
patterns.evidence_signal: The cross-session request (role B's cookies + role A's token) is accepted (same success signal TC-130.2/.3 already use: status/body matches a known-working baseline, no rejection marker) AND the state change is confirmed to have actually applied under role B specifically -- not just a 200. Requires a before/after read-back under role B's own session to distinguish 'the request was accepted' from 'the request actually mutated role B's data,' the same evidence-not-status-code discipline idor_tests.py's own confirmation helpers already apply.

stof_coverage.notes: Implemented as csrf_tests.py's _check_token_not_bound_to_session, reusing the same two-role authenticated-context pattern idor_tests.py already proved for horizontal-priv-esc (CsrfTestConfig.test_role = attacker/low-priv, .victim_role = high-priv, wired from main.py's existing low_priv_role/high_priv_role convention). For a candidate endpoint with a discovered token-shaped field: a live GET of the form as the attacker role harvests that role's own fresh token value (a small regex-based hidden-input extractor, _extract_hidden_field_value -- the HTML-form counterpart to auth_tests.py's own JSON-body _extract_token_field); the SAME state-changing POST is then submitted using the VICTIM role's own authenticated session/cookies with the attacker's token substituted into the token field, compared against a separate known-working baseline submitted under the victim's own session. Gated behind the same allow_state_changing_probes flag as TC-130.1-.3, and SKIPs cleanly (not ERROR) whenever victim_role is unconfigured, equal to test_role, JWT-authenticated, or the candidate endpoint has no token-shaped field at all -- the plan's SKIP-not-ERROR convention. Evidence bar actually met on a hit: response status/body matches a known-working same-session baseline with no rejection marker (the same status/body evidence TC-130.2/.3 already use) -- NOT a before/after read-back confirming the state change was independently observed to apply under the victim's own account, since a generic read-back isn't reliably buildable across arbitrary discovered forms; the Finding.description says so explicitly rather than overclaiming. Real-world validation against demo.testfire.net (2 roles configured: admin/normal, both form_login) produced 3x SKIP across the 3 discovered state-changing POST forms (sendFeedback, doSubscribe, bank/showTransactions) -- a legitimate, correctly-reasoned outcome, not a bug: none of this target's discovered forms has any field that looks like an anti-CSRF token at all (the same gap TC-130.1 already FAILs on for all three), so there is no token field for TC-130.4 to test a cross-session substitution against. The technique has not yet been observed to actually FAIL or PASS live against a real target with a genuine per-session token; unit tests (FAIL/PASS/SKIP-no-victim-role/SKIP-jwt-victim/SKIP-no-token-field/ERROR-harvest-failure/ERROR-baseline-failure) cover that behavior synthetically.

patterns.generalized_transformation: Diff the session/auth cookie's raw Playwright attributes (issued at login, same anon-vs-authenticated-context diff session_weakness_tests.py's TC-129.5 already uses) against the SameSite value actually set. SameSite=None is an unconditional CSRF gap by spec (RFC 6265bis): the cookie is sent on every cross-site request regardless of navigation type, so this mechanism provides zero CSRF protection on its own. SameSite=Strict is the strongest setting and blocks the classic forged cross-site form-POST outright. SameSite=Lax (Chrome/Edge/Opera's browser default since ~2020, NOT Firefox/Safari) blocks a forged cross-site POST in most modern browsers, but is not a complete CSRF defense: (1) it still allows the cookie on a top-level cross-site GET navigation, so any state change reachable via GET is unprotected; (2) Chrome's own 'Lax+POST' interim/default-cookie behavior leaves roughly a 2-minute window after a cookie is first issued where a cross-site POST still carries it (the 'SameSite Lax bypass via cookie refresh' pattern PortSwigger's own Academy lab demonstrates); (3) Firefox/Safari do not apply Lax-by-default at all, so an application relying only on the browser default (no explicit SameSite attribute) is not actually protected on those browsers.
patterns.abstracted_endpoint_pattern: The session/auth cookie identified across the same login boundary TC-129.5 already uses, cross-referenced against this module's own TC-130.1 (no anti-CSRF token field) and TC-130.3 (Origin/Referer not validated) results for the SAME discovered endpoint.
patterns.real_example: OWASP's own SameSite guidance and PortSwigger's 'Bypassing SameSite Restrictions' material (Lax-by-default nuances, the cookie-refresh 2-minute window, GET-navigation gap); RFC 6265bis (SameSite=None semantics).
patterns.evidence_signal: FAIL only when (a) SameSite=None is explicitly set (unconditional gap, no compounding needed), or (b) SameSite is Lax/absent on this endpoint's session cookie AND this same endpoint independently FAILed BOTH TC-130.1 (no token field) and TC-130.3 (Origin/Referer not validated) in the same scan pass -- a genuine compounding-risk signal (defense-in-depth is fully absent, not just one layer), not a redundant restatement of TC-129.5's own missing-HttpOnly/Secure session-hijacking framing. SameSite=Strict is never flagged.

stof_coverage.notes: Implemented as csrf_tests.py's _check_samesite_csrf_relevance / the pure helper _samesite_csrf_issue(). Reuses session_weakness_tests.py's _new_or_changed_cookies (imported directly -- both files live in stof/modules/ at the same Layer 9, and the function is pure/stateless with no I/O, so this is data reuse across sibling techniques within one layer, not the cross-layer import CLAUDE.md's boundary rule forbids) against a fresh anonymous context vs. this module's own already-authenticated context, computed ONCE per run_techniques() call (the cookie's SameSite attribute is a per-session-issuance property, not per-endpoint, so re-diffing per endpoint would be wasted work) and threaded into the per-endpoint loop alongside that endpoint's own TC-130.1/TC-130.3 outcomes. SKIPs when no session/auth cookie was identified (non-cookie-based auth) or when TC-130.1/TC-130.3 didn't run for this endpoint (their own SKIP/ERROR/gating applies uniformly first). Unit tests (SameSite=None-always-FAIL, Strict-never-flagged, Lax-only-when-compounding, absent-treated-like-Lax, SKIP-no-cookie) cover the pure helper and the full run_techniques() wiring synthetically -- 5 tests, all passing. Live validation against demo.testfire.net was attempted twice this session but BOTH runs landed all-SKIP with the 'disabled by default' gating message, not a real target-observed result: this machine had other concurrent STOF sessions actively running scans against the same config/config.json at the same time, and testing.allow_state_changing_probes is a single shared file-level flag -- each session's own finally-block auto-revert (_revert_state_changing_probes_flag) raced this module's own config reload (main.py._run_test reloads config fresh right before building modules, well after the crawl phase completes) and won both times, so the flag read back False before csrf_tests ever got to run a live probe. This is confirmed session-contention on shared repo state, not a code defect -- re-verify live once no other concurrent session holds the target/config, otherwise the correctness evidence here rests on the unit-test suite alone, consistent with TC-130.4's own prior 'not yet observed to FAIL/PASS live' honest caveat above.

patterns.generalized_transformation: For a JSON-body-shaped API endpoint (a discovered POST/PUT/PATCH endpoint_type=='api' whose parameters include at least one field the crawler tagged param_location=='body', which api_sniffer.py only does when it parsed a real application/json request body -- see api_sniffer.py's _body_param_names), resubmit the SAME already-discovered field values and the role's real session cookies but as a real HTML-form-shaped request instead of JSON: Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded via context.request.post(url, form=fields) (Playwright's normal form-encoding path, the exact same primitive TC-130.1-.4 already use), which is a content-type a plain <form> can produce with zero JavaScript. If the same success signal (_looks_like_successful_submission) fires on the form-encoded resubmission as on a JSON baseline, the endpoint's handler does not actually gate on Content-Type the way a CSRF-defense argument ('our API only accepts JSON, which a cross-site <form> can't send without JS/CORS preflight, so we're implicitly CSRF-safe') assumes -- a real, disclosed bypass class (GitLab GraphQL CVE-2024-4994, CVSS 8.1; Fastify CVE-2022-41919/GHSA-3fjj-p79j-c9hh; multiple bug-bounty JSON-to-form-urlencoded/text-plain writeups) where a lenient body parser accepts the same field data regardless of the declared Content-Type header.
patterns.abstracted_endpoint_pattern: Any discovered endpoint_type=='api' POST/PUT/PATCH endpoint with at least one crawler-observed JSON-body field -- explicitly does NOT apply to classic HTML <form>-POST endpoints (endpoint_type=='form'), which TC-130.1-.4 already cover and which never had a JSON-only content-type assumption to begin with.
patterns.real_example: CVE-2024-4994 (GitLab GraphQL endpoint accepting non-JSON content types, CVSS 8.1); CVE-2022-41919 / GHSA-3fjj-p79j-c9hh (Fastify: incorrect Content-Type parsing enabling CSRF); HackerOne report #1763832; the well-documented 'text/plain enctype' and 'x-www-form-urlencoded fallback' JSON-CSRF bypass pattern (PortSwigger, Cobalt, multiple bug-bounty writeups).
patterns.evidence_signal: A JSON baseline submission succeeds (_looks_like_successful_submission), AND the identical field data resubmitted as application/x-www-form-urlencoded via a real Playwright form POST (not fetch/XHR -- must be a shape a bare HTML <form> can actually produce) ALSO succeeds by the same signal. SKIP cleanly (not ERROR, not FAIL) whenever no JSON-body-shaped api endpoint was discovered at all -- the expected, honest outcome on a classic form-POST target like demo.testfire.net, per this module's own prior deferral note above.

stof_coverage.notes: Implemented as csrf_tests.py's _check_content_type_switch. Reuses _looks_like_successful_submission and _submit_form (form=fields path) unchanged; the JSON baseline uses context.request.post(url, data=json.dumps(fields), headers={'Content-Type': 'application/json'}). Gated behind the same allow_state_changing_probes flag as every other write-verb technique in this file, and capped at the same max_endpoints_to_probe-derived candidate list philosophy (a small, separate cap for JSON-api candidates, since they're a disjoint endpoint set from the form candidates TC-130.1-.4 probe); also independently reachable even when zero form candidates exist (run_techniques()'s own _run_content_type_switch_checks path), since it doesn't depend on TC-130.1-.5's form-endpoint gate. This was explicitly deferred in the initial csrf_tests.py wave (see this file's _meta.key_finding above) for lack of a reliably-present JSON-API endpoint on demo.testfire.net; re-verified this session against the api_sniffer.py source directly (its _body_param_names only tags param_location=='body' when it parsed a real application/json request) rather than re-deferring blind, so the SKIP path is a genuine, code-verified 'nothing to test here' rather than an assumption. Live validation against demo.testfire.net this session: two attempted scans both crawled 66-68 endpoints with 0-1 API endpoint discovered (the 1 discovered when present did not carry a crawler-observed JSON body field), so TC-130.6 would have taken its SKIP path regardless of the separate allow_state_changing_probes contention issue affecting TC-130.1-.5's own live results this session -- SKIP is the correct, expected outcome on this target. Unit tests (SKIP-no-json-endpoint, FAIL-content-type-not-gated, PASS-content-type-enforced, ERROR-json-baseline-fails, plus the pure _candidate_json_api_endpoints filter) cover FAIL/PASS synthetically since no real JSON-body endpoint exists on this target to observe live.
